selected_evidence.requirement: node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b (interfaces configured, routing enabled)
selected_evidence.summary: node1 originally had only vtnet0 (lan) configured; added opt1/opt2 (vtnet1/vtnet2) as lan-a/lan-b via config.xml edit, reconfigured, confirmed IPs assigned and IPv4 forwarding enabled

selected_evidence.requirement: End-to-end connectivity/routing between lan-a and lan-b through node1 works
selected_evidence.summary: Initial pings failed (no pass rules yet); after adding pass rules, node2 (lan-a) successfully pinged node1's lan-a gateway and node3 (lan-b) across the router

selected_evidence.requirement: TCP port 23 refused between lan-a and lan-b
selected_evidence.summary: Added block rules for tcp/23 on opt1 and opt2 (ordered before general pass rules), reloaded pf, confirmed rules loaded via pfctl, and node2's nc attempt to node3:23 timed out (blocked)

selected_evidence.requirement: Refused attempts are logged on node1, with an entry produced by an attempt from node2
selected_evidence.summary: filterlog entry captured: block,in on vtnet1, tcp, source 10.50.1.11 (node2) dest 10.50.2.12 (node3) port 23, tagged with the block-telnet rule label, matching node2's nc attempt

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline before restart
selected_evidence.summary: Captured node1 kern.boottime (1781492144), pf state table active, opt1/opt2 interface addresses present before restart

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnect, then native reboot
selected_evidence.summary: shutdown -r now issued in background; ack_sent returned before the connection dropped

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: polled until available, changed boot identity proven
selected_evidence.summary: Connection timed out during reboot, then kern.boottime returned as 1788626353 (changed from 1781492144), proving an actual reboot occurred

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: post-restart recovery of services/data (firewall config, logging)
selected_evidence.summary: opt1/opt2 interfaces and block/pass pf rules reloaded automatically from config.xml on boot; new day's filter log created; a fresh block+log demonstration from node2 succeeded post-restart

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 0472ca1f-...; reboot ack accepted; post-restart boot_id 947cc78b-... (changed); eth1 restored and ping to node1's lan-a gateway succeeded, confirming recovery

selected_evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline captured and acknowledgement sent, but post-restart recovery unverifiable (explicit limitation)
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id ae466ddb-... captured before restart; reboot command's ack_sent was returned; node3 remained unreachable (connection reset by peer / timed out) on every poll for over 30 minutes afterward while node1/node2 continued responding normally, so a changed boot identity and recovered state could not be confirmed for node3

import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET, shutil
path = '/conf/config.xml'
shutil.copy(path, path + '.bak1')
tree = ET.parse(path)
root = tree.getroot()
ifaces = root.find('interfaces')

def mk_iface(name, physif, descr, ip, subnet):
    el = ET.SubElement(ifaces, name)
    ET.SubElement(el, 'enable').text = '1'
    ET.SubElement(el, 'if').text = physif
    ET.SubElement(el, 'descr').text = descr
    ET.SubElement(el, 'ipaddr').text = ip
    ET.SubElement(el, 'subnet').text = str(subnet)
    ET.SubElement(el, 'spoofmac').text = ''
    return el

mk_iface('opt2', 'vtnet2', 'lan-b', '10.50.2.254', 24)

commands.command:
cat > /tmp/add_rules.py <<'PY'
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET, shutil
path = '/conf/config.xml'
shutil.copy(path, path + '.bak2')
tree = ET.parse(path)
root = tree.getroot()
filt = root.find('filter')

def add_block_telnet(iface, descr):
    rule = ET.SubElement(filt, 'rule')
    ET.SubElement(rule, 'type').text = 'block'
    ET.SubElement(rule, 'ipprotocol').text = 'inet'
    ET.SubElement(rule, 'protocol').text = 'tcp'
    ET.SubElement(rule, 'interface').text = iface
    ET.SubElement(rule, 'log').text = '1'
    ET.SubElement(rule, 'descr').text = descr
    src = ET.SubElement(rule, 'source')
    ET.SubElement(src, 'any')
    dst = ET.SubElement(rule, 'destination')
    ET.SubElement(dst, 'any')
    ET.SubElement(dst, 'port').text = '23'
    return rule

def add_pass_any(iface, netname, descr):
    rule = ET.SubElement(filt, 'rule')
    ET.SubElement(rule, 'type').text = 'pass'
    ET.SubElement(rule, 'ipprotocol').text = 'inet'
    ET.SubElement(rule, 'interface').text = iface
    ET.SubElement(rule, 'descr').text = descr
    src = ET.SubElement(rule, 'source')
    ET.SubElement(src, 'network').text = netname
    dst = ET.SubElement(rule, 'destination')
    ET.SubElement(dst, 'any')
    return rule

# Block rules first (evaluated in order, quick semantics for interface rules)
add_block_telnet('opt1', 'antrieb: block telnet lan-a to lan-b')
add_block_telnet('opt2', 'antrieb: block telnet lan-b to lan-a')
# Then general pass rules for routed traffic between the two LANs / to any
add_pass_any('opt1', 'opt1', 'antrieb: allow lan-a to any except telnet')
add_pass_any('opt2', 'opt2', 'antrieb: allow lan-b to any except telnet')

tree.write(path, xml_declaration=True, encoding='utf-8')
print('rules added')
PY
